title: Codegen Internals
concept: Codegen translates the typed AST into LLVM Intermediate Representation — the bridge between XIOM semantics and machine code generation.
why: Understanding codegen reveals how your high-level XIOM code becomes low-level machine instructions. It explains performance characteristics and optimizations.
syntax_ref:
# View generated LLVM IR:
xiom build --emit-ir main.xi

# LLVM IR basics:
# %name = operation type operand1, operand2
# br i1 %cond, label %true_branch, label %false_branch
# ret type %value
tips: Use --emit-ir to understand how your code compiles — invaluable for optimization
SSA form means every variable is assigned once — the codegen inserts phi nodes for control flow merges
Struct field access becomes GEP (GetElementPtr) instructions — pointer arithmetic by the LLVM
Tail-recursive functions often compile to loops — check the IR to verify
common_mistakes: Assuming direct mapping: one XIOM line ≠ one LLVM IR line
Forgetting that debug builds include extra code for contract checks and overflow detection
Reading LLVM IR without understanding SSA — phi nodes look confusing without context
